title: Isolation Forest Transfer: Applying Unsupervised Anomaly Detection from Cybersecurity to Agent Action Streams

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Unsupervised methods that require only benign baselines are more deployable than supervised monitors. Quantifying the unsupervised vs. supervised trade-off directly informs practical monitoring deployment decisions where labeled malicious data is scarce.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Isolation forest is 5 lines of scikit-learn. Feature engineering (tool call frequency, action distribution, timing) is basic data processing. No GPU needed. Comparing AUC between unsupervised and supervised is standard ML evaluation. Ideal for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Featurize trajectories, train isolation forest on 100 benign, evaluate on SHADE-Arena. Single algorithm, single comparison. The deliverable is an AUC comparison table. Could be done in under 10 hours of implementation. Extremely well-scoped.

title: Honeypot-Inspired Canary Actions: Importing Network Security Deception Techniques for AI Monitoring

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Canary/honeypot techniques are a fundamentally different monitoring paradigm: passive, near-zero false positive rate, no reasoning analysis needed. title: SCADA Defense-in-Depth Transfer: Implementing Tiered Access Control as a Monitoring Complement
original_idea: Implement tiered action permission system in ControlArena (analogous to SCADA zone crossings) where agents escalate privilege for higher-risk actions. Add a monitor watching privilege escalation events. Evaluate whether privilege-escalation monitoring catches more SHADE-Arena sabotage attempts than general-action monitoring with lower false positive rate.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear causal chain: focused monitoring on rare high-risk events (privilege escalations) should yield better precision than monitoring all actions. The SCADA analogy provides a validated theoretical basis, and the prediction (higher detection fraction, lower FPR) is testable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Implementing tiered permissions in ControlArena is a non-trivial software engineering task. Beginner CS students would need guidance on both SCADA concepts and ControlArena internals. Feasible in 30hrs but tight. No heavy compute needed.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Requires both implementing the tiered system AND building a monitor AND running comparisons. The scope includes infrastructure work plus evaluation, making it broader than a single experiment.

title: Behavioral Baseline Profiling Transfer: Importing UEBA for AI Agent Profiling
original_idea: Run a fixed LLM agent on 30 benign ControlArena tasks to establish behavioral baseline (action distribution, timing, error rate). Monitor the same agent on SHADE-Arena tasks using deviation from personal baseline rather than absolute thresholds. Compare detection AUC of baseline-deviation monitor vs. absolute-threshold monitor.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear theory: per-agent baselines outperform absolute thresholds in cybersecurity because normal behavior varies across entities. The prediction (higher AUC for baseline-deviation monitor) is directly testable and safety-relevant.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Straightforward implementation: run agent on benign tasks, collect statistics, compute deviations. No ML training needed. Standard Python. Fits well in 30hrs for beginners. Medium compute sufficient for the ~60 agent runs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-defined: establish baseline on N tasks, test on SHADE-Arena tasks, compare AUC. Single clear experiment with a defined metric (AUC comparison). Deliverable is a comparison chart.

title: Tripwire-Based Monitoring Transfer: Static Environment Integrity Checks from Security Operations
original_idea: In ControlArena bash tasks, implement a file/environment state integrity monitor that checksums critical files before and after each agent step. Flag any modification to resources the agent was not supposed to modify. Compare tripwire-based monitor to standard LLM action monitor on SHADE-Arena sabotage tasks.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong theory: tripwire monitoring catches sabotage results regardless of how the agent hides its actions. This is a fundamentally different monitoring paradigm (state-based vs. action-based) with clear safety implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Checksumming files is basic Python (hashlib). No ML required. Very accessible for beginner CS students. Minimal compute. Well within 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tight scope: implement checksumming, run on SHADE-Arena bash tasks, compare to LLM monitor. Single well-defined experiment. Only minor ambiguity around which files to monitor.

title: Red Team / Blue Team Exercise Transfer: Structured Adversarial Monitoring Improvement
original_idea: Design and conduct a small-scale red/blue team exercise in ControlArena: one participant modifies SHADE-Arena sabotage strategies to evade a standard monitor; the other improves the monitor to detect evasion. Run 3-5 rounds. Document findings as a case study.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reasonable theory that adversarial pressure improves monitoring robustness, but the output is a qualitative case study rather than a quantified safety-relevant result. The causal chain to safety improvement is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires both designing attack strategies and improving monitors iteratively. Needs understanding of both SHADE-Arena attack mechanisms and monitor internals. Guided beginners could manage but it demands creativity and AI safety domain knowledge.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Open-ended by design: each round produces unpredictable outcomes that shape the next round. No fixed deliverable or metric. 3-5 rounds of adversarial interaction is broad and hard to scope tightly.

title: Mutual Information Monitor: Measuring Information Leakage as an AI Safety Signal
original_idea: In ControlArena tasks with simulated sensitive data, estimate mutual information between agent outputs and locations of sensitive data. Compare MI-based anomaly score between benign and malicious SHADE-Arena trajectories. Implement using k-NN based MI estimator.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong theoretical grounding: MI is a principled measure of information leakage from information theory. Clear safety-relevant prediction: MI should separate benign from malicious trajectories if exfiltration is occurring.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Estimating MI between high-dimensional agent outputs and environment state is non-trivial. k-NN MI estimators require careful parameter tuning and understanding of information theory. Beginner CS students would struggle significantly with this. Defining the right random variables is itself challenging.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Reasonably scoped (compute MI, compare benign vs malicious) but significant ambiguity in how to represent agent outputs and sensitive data locations as random variables for MI estimation.

title: Counterfactual Monitoring: Would the Agent Have Taken the Same Action Without the Malicious Instruction?
original_idea: For each SHADE-Arena task, run the agent on benign main task only (no malicious side task). Record actions. Then run with malicious side task included. Flag actions appearing only in the malicious run. Measure precision and recall of this counterfactual monitor.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Excellent theoretical grounding: counterfactual reasoning is the gold standard for causal attribution. The approach directly tests whether actions are caused by malicious instructions, which is the core safety question. Falsifiable prediction with clear metrics.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Conceptually simple: run agent twice (with and without malicious instruction), compare outputs. No ML training needed. Standard Python comparison. Medium compute for the paired runs. Well-suited for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-defined experiment: paired runs, diff the action sequences, compute precision/recall. Clear deliverable. Minor ambiguity in how to match actions across runs (exact match vs fuzzy).

title: Petri Net Formalization: Modeling AI Agent Control Flows for Deadlock and Unsafe State Detection
original_idea: Model one ControlArena task's control flow as a Petri net. Define unsafe states. Use reachability analysis to determine if unsafe states are reachable. Compare formally identified unsafe states to those caught by the LLM monitor on actual trajectories.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong theory: formal verification can prove certain unsafe states are unreachable, providing stronger guarantees than empirical monitoring. Clear causal chain from formal model to safety guarantee.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Petri net modeling requires formal methods knowledge that beginner CS students typically lack. Learning the Petri tool, formalizing a task as a Petri net, and performing reachability analysis is a steep learning curve for beginners within 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Nicely scoped to one task. Clear deliverable: a Petri net model with reachability analysis results compared to monitor outputs. The single-task constraint keeps it narrow.

title: Online Learning Monitor: Adapting IDS Adaptive Baselining to Continuously Update AI Monitor Thresholds
original_idea: Implement EWMA baseline updater for AI agent behavioral metrics in ControlArena. Compare static-threshold vs adaptive-threshold monitor on a scenario where the agent is updated mid-deployment. Measure detection rate and false alarm rate before and after the update.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reasonable theory: adaptive thresholds should handle distribution shift better than static ones. Safety-relevant for deployment, but the causal chain is somewhat indirect (better adaptation -> fewer false alarms -> more trusted monitoring).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: EWMA is a simple formula. Implementation is straightforward Python. Simulating an agent update mid-deployment is just changing the model config. Fits well in 30hrs for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-defined: implement EWMA, run pre/post update experiment, compare metrics. Clear deliverable (detection rate and FAR comparison chart). Single experimental design.

title: Minimum Description Length Monitor: Compression-Based Anomaly Detection for AI Agent Behavior
original_idea: Represent agent trajectories as strings over action type vocabulary. Compute compression ratio using gzip/zstd. Establish baseline from 100 benign METR traces. Flag SHADE-Arena trajectories outside baseline distribution. Evaluate AUC and compare to isolation forest.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reasonable theory: compression captures structural regularity, and malicious trajectories may have unusual structure. But the connection between compression ratio and safety-relevant behavior is indirect and may not hold if malicious actions are structurally similar to benign ones.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Trivially simple implementation: import gzip, compress strings, compare ratios. No ML needed for the main approach. Isolation forest comparison is one scikit-learn call. Very accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Extremely narrow: compress trajectories, compute ratios, compare distributions, report AUC. Single clear experiment with a single deliverable metric.

title: Nuclear Safety Barrier Transfer: Modeling AI Control Protocols as Defense-in-Depth Barrier Chains
original_idea: Model a ControlArena control protocol as a chain of barriers (input sanitization, monitoring, sandboxing, human review, audit). Estimate each barrier's failure probability from experimental data. Compute overall system failure probability. Identify the weakest barrier.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-defined: model barriers, estimate probabilities, compute overall failure rate, identify weakest link. Clear deliverable (barrier analysis table with recommendations). Minor scope ambiguity in how to estimate some probabilities.

title: Behavioral Fingerprinting Transfer: Using Browser Fingerprinting Techniques to Distinguish Compromised AI Agent States
original_idea: Extract 20+ weak behavioral signals from agent trajectories. Combine into a behavioral fingerprint vector. Train a one-class SVM on benign fingerprints. Evaluate fingerprint deviation as anomaly score on SHADE-Arena malicious trajectories. Compare to single-feature monitors.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reasonable theory that combining many weak signals outperforms single signals, validated in fingerprinting contexts. But the connection to safety is somewhat indirect -- this is really an anomaly detection approach with a security analogy.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Extracting 20+ behavioral features requires significant feature engineering effort and domain knowledge about what constitutes a meaningful signal. One-class SVM is in scikit-learn, but the feature extraction step is the bottleneck for beginners. Feasible in 30hrs but demanding.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Reasonably scoped but the 20+ features requirement introduces significant design decisions. Each feature needs to be defined, extracted, and validated. The comparison to single-feature monitors adds another dimension.

title: Benign Baseline Coverage Analysis: Measuring How Well METR/MALT Benign Tasks Cover Real Deployments
original_idea: Sample 50 tasks from METR and 50 from MALT. Characterize each by domain, tool diversity, task length, reversibility, and sensitive resource presence. Compare to real-world AI agent use cases. Identify gaps. Estimate impact on monitor calibration.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: No ML needed, just labeling and statistical comparison. Scraping real-world use cases is straightforward. Accessible for beginners. Fits in 30hrs easily. No compute requirements.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sampling and characterizing 100 tasks is well-defined, but the comparison to real-world use cases introduces subjectivity in what constitutes a representative sample. 'Estimate impact on monitor calibration' is vague.

title: Cross-Monitor Agreement Benchmark: Measuring When Multiple Monitoring Approaches Disagree
original_idea: Run 4 monitoring methods (keyword filter, LLM monitor, isolation forest, CUSUM) on all SHADE-Arena public trajectories. Compute pairwise agreement rates and Cohen's kappa. Identify disagreement cases. Analyze whether disagreement predicts lower ensemble performance. Propose ensemble combination rule.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Reasonable theory: inter-monitor agreement reveals complementarity and guides ensemble design. Useful for practical monitoring but the safety-relevant insight is indirect (better ensembles -> better detection).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running 4 different monitoring methods requires setting up each one, which is non-trivial. Keyword filter and CUSUM are simple, but isolation forest needs feature extraction and LLM monitor needs API calls. Feasible but demanding for beginners in 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Setting up 4 monitors, computing agreement, analyzing disagreement cases, and proposing ensemble rules is a lot of surface area. Each monitor setup is its own sub-project. Moderately scoped.
